questions.question: Q27
questions.title: 400 GB database restore still running
questions.why: to a person (Mohnish Grover, 15 Nov 2026); reasoning drafted by Gemini and approved by Mohnish Grover, see recheck_15nov
questions.note: CHANGE NEEDED: new question rule - a database restore still running long after it started -> person (article gives ~10 min per 100 GB; a stalled restore is on CloudServe's side). Must not catch questions about how to start a restore

words: to a person
Gemini but approved by me
reasoning_drafted_by_gemini_approved_by_: No way to check live status. The article says to allow "roughly ten minutes per hundred gigabytes" (around 40 minutes for 400 GB, or much longer under load). However, if the restore has been running for hours, the customer cannot tell from this article whether it is just slow or genuinely hung—only support can check the backend job.
Risk of data loss or downtime. Customers dealing with active database restores often need reassurance before they cancel or retry a job.

standing_rules: Never change Ines's words (Mohnish Grover, 14 Nov 2026).
If the answer is split across two articles, the reply should draw on both (Mohnish Grover, 14 Nov 2026).
If an automatic answer did not solve the problem, the follow-up goes to a person with a draft (Mohnish Grover, 14 Nov 2026).
general_changes: Follow-ups: link a new ticket to the same customer's recent automatic reply on the same type (customer_id, date, 7-day window) and send it to a person with a draft (the earlier reply, article and what was not certain), instead of answering again.

general_changes.rule: plan rule: when an article the reply uses applies only to other plans ('Applies to' line), the ticket goes to a person with the draft
general_changes.words: It should be a general rule because if the standard plan customers cannot get their answers with it then it will be useless (Mohnish Grover)

general_changes.rule: handover: a plain-code summary for every ticket sent to a person (what it is about, the customer's words, why, the documents, what the system was not sure about); no question numbers in what the agent reads; a draft for tickets sent to a person by his own decisions; 'draft' only holds a reply that could be sent
